description: 5 exemplars + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-10 under road-to-corpus-refresh-cadence-shape 1.2c, which stamped this skill's grounding corpus and so brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. `last_eval` carries the authoring date, not a live eval result — the convention this tree already follows (see 1.2a's and 1.2b's notes on the same field); no live trigger eval ran for this file. Exemplars cover the explicit tuning request and the implicit one this skill's own description names verbatim ('this query is slow'), plus indexing strategy, a multi-connection question, and the German equivalent. Near-misses are three neighbours that share database vocabulary and are still somebody else's job: two are named in this skill's SKILL.md 'Do NOT use when' block — ORM model work and a migration-only ask — and the third, schema review against the persistence rule surface, is included because it reads as a database question and routes to schema-review. Counterexamples guard the 'database' homonym: a vector store used as an embedding index rather than a relational engine, and a hosting/billing question that names the database without asking anything about its behaviour.

queries.note: the implicit form this skill's own description names verbatim

queries.q: EXPLAIN shows a seq scan on a 40M row table even though the WHERE is selective — what index do I need?
we paginate with OFFSET and page 8000 takes four seconds — how should this actually be done?
should the read replica get its own connection pool, or share the primary's?
die Abfrage auf der Bestelltabelle ist viel zu langsam — welcher Index fehlt da?
add a hasMany relation to the Order model and set up the inverse
queries.note: ORM model work, which this skill's SKILL.md names in its 'Do NOT use when' block → the framework's own skill (eloquent / symfony-workflow / framework-native)

queries.q: write the migration that adds the status column to orders
queries.note: migration-only, named in the same 'Do NOT use when' block → the framework-specific migration skill

queries.q: review this schema change against the persistence rules before it ships
queries.note: reads as a database question and is a review against the scale-discipline rule surface → schema-review, which runs lint_persistence and emits the gap table

queries.q: which vector database should we use for the embedding index — pgvector, Qdrant or Pinecone?
queries.note: the 'database' homonym: a vector store chosen as an embedding index, not relational architecture or query behaviour

queries.q: our managed database bill doubled this month — can you work out which plan we are on?
queries.note: names the database and asks nothing about its behaviour; this is a hosting and billing question
